replication.target_description: Located test on p. 27: direct path from extraversion to total screen time in parallel mediation model (life satisfaction outcome; additional active/passive social media mediators), university students. Total screen time includes non-social-media activities, so the outcome does not match time spent using social media.

n.sample_role: University student participants; exact analytic n for the parallel mediation target path is not printed unambiguously
n.exclusions: Missing values automatically removed from analyses; approximately 50 participants excluded in most analyses (p. 36). Recruitment N=149 is not analytic n; no n inferred from df.
n.location: pp. 20, 35–36; target parallel mediation on pp. 27–28
n.quote: A total number of 149 participants were recruited. / missing values which were automatically removed from the analyses

es.location: p. 27, Parallel Mediation analysis; p. 28, Table 3, TST row
es.quote: only the direct effect on Total Screen Time was negative and significant [B = -0.41, SE = 0.12, t (1, 94) = -3.38, p < .05]

p.location: p. 28, Table 3, Direct effects of Extraversion on, TST row, p-value column

reported_success.location: p. 32, Discussion: comparison of extraversion/screen-time direction
reported_success.quote: instead of increasing extraversion levels leading to increased screen time, in the current study, the higher the extraversion level, the less time is spent on screens.

notes: Replication locator identifies total screen time, not social media time; target_match=false. Narrative verdict is scoped to the authors’ directional comparison for this changed operationalization. Table 3 gives exact p=.001; p. 27 prose gives only p<.05 for the same path. Original sample reporting is internally inconsistent (usable N=304 and Table 2 N=304 versus regression F(1,417)); analytic n left null. Original beta extracted as labeled, without assuming standardization or converting metrics.
